Announcement · Flightcast × Amazon Music

Video is coming to Amazon Music.

A new place for people to watch your show, and the marketing that comes with it.

Prepared for Flightcast creators · Four marketing programmes from Amazon Music

Amazon Music is about to start showing video podcasts. That is a new place for people to watch your show, inside an app they already open every day for music and podcasts.

What it means for your show

  • People will be able to watch your show on Amazon Music, not just listen to it
  • If you already publish video through Flightcast, your episodes will be there automatically. There is nothing separate to upload

This is how a video episode looks to someone on Amazon Music.

And Flightcast can get you into the marketing that comes with it. Amazon is opening four marketing programmes to a small number of shows, and we think yours is one of them. Here is where your show could show up.

The free tier
01The big one

A billboard in Times Square

Best for shows with a big audience already. 3 to 4 months lead time.

A week on one of the world’s biggest screens, plus a shoot you keep.

What you get

  • A one-week feature on Amazon Music's billboard at 20 Times Square, full-screen video
  • Professionally captured photography and video, yours to use on social
  • A featured spot inside the Amazon Music app
  • Amazon's own ad spend behind the files you give them, as set out in the social ads section below

Photographs: previous Amazon Music features on the boards at Times Square.

What they want back

  • Website: a button or link on your site pointing to your show on Amazon Music
  • Audio: an ad at the start of your episodes, played 750,000 times, naming Amazon Music and no other platform
  • Social: one Instagram feed post tagging @amazonmusic using the photos from the shoot. The account posting it needs at least 250,000 followers
  • Display: a banner campaign seen at least 100,000 times, linking to your show on Amazon Music
  • Newsletter: an email to at least 100,000 people, pointing them to Amazon Music and no other platform
  • A video of you, 15 to 30 seconds, talking about the show
  • A headshot you are happy with, which they use to build a still image ad
  • Cover art at 3000 × 3000 pixels, JPG, or MOV if you want it to loop
  • A tagline, 40 characters or less
02Quickest

Being featured in the Amazon Music app

About 3 weeks from sending it over to going live.

It reaches people already looking for something to listen to.

What you get

Amazon puts your show in front of people browsing the app. That might be a spot at the top of a page, or a place on one of their themed lists. How prominent it is comes down to Amazon's team, who look at how big your audience is, how good the show is, and how well it fits what they are pushing at the time.

To ask for this, fill in Amazon's partner promotional request form: airtable.com/partner promotional request

What they want back

Nothing. You are not promising them anything for this one.

03No money changes hands

Swap ad space with Amazon Music

You trade ad space you already have for ad space you could not buy.

What you get

Ads for your show play to people using the free version of Amazon Music. That is their whole free audience, including plenty of people who have never come across your show.

What they want back

An ad telling your own listeners that the show is on Amazon Music, played 2 million times across your episodes.

How it works

  1. You record an audio ad pointing your listeners to your show on Amazon Music
  2. You run it in your own episodes, the same way you would run any other ad, until it has been played 2 million times
  3. Amazon runs ads for your show to people on the free tier of Amazon Music
  4. Nobody pays anybody. It is ad space for ad space

How long the 2 million takes is down to your download numbers. A show doing 100,000 downloads an episode gets there faster than one doing 10,000, so it is worth working out your own timeline before committing.

04Costs you nothing

Ads on social, paid for by Amazon

Full details overleaf. Usually live within a week.

Someone else pays, and clips you already posted can do the work.

What you get

Amazon pays for ads promoting your show on social media. It does not cost you anything. There are three things you can give them, and you can do more than one.

What they want back: any of these three

  • A video of you. Record 15 to 30 seconds talking about your show on Amazon Music, and they run it with their ad money across social. Filmed wide or upright, either is fine
  • A headshot. You send one you have approved, they use it to build a still image ad
  • Clips from your episodes, 30 seconds or less. No need to film anything new. Clips you have already posted on social are fine

The social ads, in detail

You send Amazon the videos and photos, they pay to run them as ads on TikTok, Instagram and Facebook. The ads go out under your name and Amazon's at the same time, so they reach more people but still look like they came from you, and they do not clutter up your own feed. Every ad links back to your show. Send all three kinds if you can. You need a professional or business Instagram account to take part on Instagram and Facebook. Any TikTok account works.

Filming it

  • Plain background, camera on something steady. Not handheld, not a selfie
  • Having your mic and headphones in shot works well

The file

  • 15 to 30 seconds long, under 500 MB
  • Upright, wide or square all work
  • Add subtitles if you can. Amazon adds the closing frame

What to say

  • Say who you are, then what the show is: the sort of conversations you have, a story that would make someone stop and listen
  • Keep it general so it does not date. No naming particular episodes or guests
  • Finish with "Listen to the podcast now on Amazon Music", or "Watch the podcast now on Amazon Music" if you make video

The still image ad

  • One good, high-resolution headshot. Amazon builds the ad around it and links it to your show

Clips from the show

  • 30 seconds or less, taken from video episodes that are already on Amazon Music
  • Clips you have already posted are fine

Where the ads go

Facebook, Threads, Instagram, TikTok

When they start

Usually within a week of you sending the files

How long they run

4 to 6 weeks, and up to 3 to 6 months if they are working

How often to send

No fixed schedule. 1 to 4 a month suits them best

What you hear back

Everything you send does get run and does get seen. Amazon will not tell you how many people clicked through and listened, as a matter of their policy
